commits.message:
Each part reads its own grounds; a seam's divider fits it under every caps (rich-joiners-9ntp.13i)

High review pass on #406:
- A seam decides its endpoints from the grounds the seam and divider read,
  a lead or tail from the one it reads, so caps that need a ground no longer
  stop a seam that needs none (plain + capsule dropped every " | ").
- parseSeam holds the divider to the seam's width under every caps (own cells'
  width and each cap's count equal), so a parsed seam is valid with any caps.
- A cell naming a cap and drawing a glyph is refused, not silently reduced.
- Refusals name the argument (`seam:` / `caps:`), not `CellJoiner:`.
- joinerNamed refuses a spec that is neither a name nor { seam, caps }.
- Private Use Area glyphs back to \u escapes, as master had them.

A joiner is a seam and caps picked independently (rich-joiners-9ntp.13i)

CellJoiner takes a JoinSeam (the middle) and a JoinCaps (the ends), each
with its glyph and ascii forms, so any seam ends in any caps: SEAMS.prism
with CAPS.bubble is one constructor call, and joinerNamed reads
{ seam, caps } from config beside a JOINERS name. A seam cell may be
{ cap: "lead" | "tail" }, so the seams that part their runs (capsule,
wrapper, metro) end them in whatever caps they are joined with.
gradientSeam replaces gradientJoiner.

Every JOINERS preset and the gradient render byte-identically to before
(truecolor, 16-colour and ASCII, checked against a pre-change snapshot).

A split host holds ESC ESC for the byte that decides it (rich-unfiled-791c.hyfo) (#405)

* A split host holds ESC ESC for the byte that decides it (rich-unfiled-791c.hyfo)

macOS Terminal sends Option+Up as `ESC ESC [ A`. On a split host a read
that ended after `ESC ESC` was consumed at once as one Escape, so no hold
was armed and the rest arrived as `[` and `A`.

`ESC ESC` alone is now unfinished like `ESC [` alone: held for the escape
delay on a split host, settled at the chunk's end on a whole-keys host.
`reissue` reads it as one Escape, so the double-send rule has one home
whether the sequence stalls or is ended by a byte that cannot extend it.

* ESC ESC that opens no key is one Escape, whatever follows it (rich-unfiled-791c.hyfo)

A stalled ESC ESC O on a split host read as Escape, Alt+O, and ESC ESC
before a sequence cut short as two Escapes, while ESC ESC before any
other byte was one. reissue now reads ESC ESC as the one double-sent
Escape at any length; only a pointer report keeps the second ESC.

Frames of content play on a beat for a time the host hands in (rich-animation-xi28.a3n)

`beat(holds)` joins the easing vocabulary: holds in seconds, looped on
`Phase.loop`, the hold in progress out, so a sequence of unequal holds is one
beat and `steps(n)` is its equal-holds case. `Frames` draws the frame in
progress at a handed `t` — every frame at the widest one's width, ending no
line, each frame its own `RichText` — and `animationFuncs(frameTime)` registers
`frames <seconds> <frame> …` for a template, the time read when it is evaluated.

Nothing reads a clock; holds are seconds, never frame counts, and both are
tested sampled once a second and sixty times a second. A 120-column row holding
the frames renders at 0.015 ms p50 at t = 0 and at t = 10⁶ s.
